task: Bug: `tenacity.after_log` crashes with `TypeError` when `retry_state.seconds_since_start` is `None` (it is `None` when the outcome timestamp has not been set). The log message should still be emitted, showing "?" in place of the elapsed seconds.
why:
All four candidates make the same fix in `tenacity/after.py` (c4 only names the variable differently), so the choice came down to test quality and lint. c3 and c4 write `f"after ?(s), "`, an f-string with no placeholders. That is a pyflakes F541 error under the repo's ruff config (`select` includes "F"), which the test-only gates don't run. ruff isn't installed here, so I didn't run it; this is from reading the config.
The runner-up, c2, is lint-clean, but it adds `RetryCallState`/`Retrying` imports and builds the state by hand instead of using the existing `make_retry_state` helper.
c1 uses the existing helper, sets `outcome_timestamp = None`, asserts the exact "?" message, and adds nothing else.
